title: Graceful limiter blackout handling and fair burst redistribution
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Problem: We observed two incidents where the central admission limiter experienced transient unreliability during a regional network partition. Symptoms: sudden 5-15s tail latencies, request error spikes, and disproportionate token shedding affecting a small set of high-burst tenants. Root cause hypothesis: ephemeral state loss in the limiter (lease/meta store timeouts) combined with naive proportional shedding led to unfair long-tail client degradation. Goals: (1) ensure graceful blackouts of limiter nodes with deterministic, low-latency failover, (2) maintain per-tenant fairness during burst absorption, and (3) provide clear operational signal and automated fallback that preserves SLOs for high-priority tenants.
proposal_summary: Introduce an ephemeral-lease broker layer and a loss-tolerant reconciliation path. The broker maintains lightweight, replicated lease fragments per-tenant (in-memory + sticky raft-lite) to enable instant admission decisions if central store is unreachable. On detection of limiter outage, the broker triggers a coordinated degradation: (a) bounded per-tenant burst buckets with time-decayed credits, (b) probabilistic fair-drop arbitration favoring long-tail low-rate tenants, and (c) precomputed model variants for severe degradation. Add circuit-breaker hysteresis and an emergency proportionate-shed policy that respects tenant SLO tiers.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Broker vs full replicated store: choose broker to avoid heavy write amplification and keep failover fast, accepting eventual consistency during long partitions.
- Prefetching vs on-demand: prefetch heatmap for top N tenants per region to minimize cold-start unfairness; increases memory but reduces burst loss.
- Deterministic vs probabilistic eviction: probabilistic fair-drop reduces coordinated synchronized retries but introduces variance in a single-tenanted percents; deterministic round-robin would penalize large numbers of mid-priority tenants.
- Complexity: adds broker component and raft-lite; trade increased operational surface for faster recovery and smoother fairness guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Limiter blackout simulation (loss of central store) shows <1% additional error rate for P0 tenants over a 5m outage in test harness
Burst absorption test with 10x baseline traffic for top-100 tenants keeps median latency within SLO and maintains fairness index (Jain index > 0.85) compared to current baseline
Canary rollout plan exists with automated rollback on SLO regressions triggered by dashboard alert
Runbook updated with recovery steps and playbook for broker node replacement
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for lease broker state transitions and probabilistic arbitration. 2) Integration test in staging with simulated central store timeouts and cross-region packet loss. 3) Chaos test: kill limiter nodes during high-burst synthetic traffic using k6 and observe shedding patterns. 4) Performance benchmark: measure additional P50/P95 overhead introduced by broker lookup (target <2ms median).
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: broker_lease_hit_ratio, broker_fallback_rate, proportionate_shed_rate_by_tier, fairness_jain_index, limiter_reconcile_latency. Alerts: broker_fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained for 2m; fairness_jain_index < 0.8; emergency_shed_active for >1m. Dashboards: per-region and per-tenant breakdown plus top-100 tenant heatmap. Linked dashboard: https://dashboard.redwood.internal/d/limiters/blackout-fairness
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy broker to canary region (us-west2) behind feature flag. 2) Run synthetic burst suite for 24h. 3) Gradual region-by-region rollout with 10% traffic shift increments and 1h observation windows. 4) Full rollout if no SLO regressions after 72h. Automated rollback on either: (a) P0 error rate spike >2x, (b) fairness_jain_index drop below 0.75, (c) broker_reconcile_latency > 50ms.
migration_and_backward_compatibility: Broker falls back to central store when available. For backward compatibility, legacy limiter nodes accept broker-delegated lease handoffs over existing admission protocol (no client changes). Migration will be staged by tenant tier: test tenants -> non-critical tenants -> P1 -> P0.
open_questions:
- Exact size and eviction policy for prefetch heatmap (memory tradeoff).
- Whether to make probabilistic arbitration parameter per-tenant or global.
- Runbook authority for manual overrides—who can toggle emergency proportionate-shed for a tenant?
security_considerations: Lease tokens are ephemeral and scoped; use short-lived mTLS between brokers and limiter nodes. No tenant secrets are stored in broker memory. KMS integration not required for broker token rotation but audit logs will include broker decisions for compliance. Security review: informal review completed with Security team on 2026-02-25 (feedback incorporated).
